facts.statement: Sikannisuchus is an extinct genus of large archosaurs found in the Upper Triassic of northeastern British Columbia, Canada.
facts.quote: Sikannisuchus is an extinct genus of large archosaur from upper Triassic (Norian stage) deposits of northeastern British Columbia, Canada.

facts.statement: The genus is known from the holotype specimen TMP 94.382.3, which consists of a posterior portion of the skull roof and other fragmentary remains.
facts.quote: It is known from the holotype, TMP 94.382.3, a posterior portion of skull roof and from other fragmentary remains.

facts.statement: Sikannisuchus would have reached a length of about 4 meters.
facts.quote: It would have reached about 4 m in length.

facts.statement: Fossils were found at four localities within the Pardonet Formation near the community of Sikanni Chief.
facts.quote: It was found from four localities of the Pardonet Formation, near the community of Sikanni Chief.

facts.statement: The genus was first named by Elizabeth L. Nicholls, Donald B. Brinkman, and Xiao-Chun Wu in 1998, with Sikannisuchus huskyi as the type species.
facts.quote: It was first named by Elizabeth L. Nicholls, Donald B. Brinkman, and Xiao-Chun Wu in 1998 and the type species is Sikannisuchus huskyi.

facts.statement: Sikannisuchus is classified within the order Archosauria, subclass Archosauromorpha, and class Reptilia.
facts.quote: subclassis: Archosauromorpha classis: Reptilia infraclassis: Archosauriformes unranked_ordo: Archosauria

facts.statement: Sikannisuchus lived during the Norian stage of the Triassic, between 227.3 and 205.7 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Norian to Norian (227.3 to 205.7 million years ago)

facts.statement: The Pardonet Formation, where Sikannisuchus fossils were found, also contains ichthyosaurs, coelacanths, and various molluscs.
facts.quote: Ichthyosaurs such as Macgowania, Callawayia and possibly the giant shastasaurid Shonisaurus, coelacanths Whiteia banffensis and possibly Garnbergia, and various genera of molluscs including ammonites and bivalves have also been found in the Pardonet Formation.
